q: Momentum (p) of a body is defined as the ____, which is written as $p=mv$.
c: product of the mass of the body and its velocity
e: Momentum (p) of a body is defined as the product of the mass of the body and its velocity, which is written as $p=mv$. Product of the mass of the body and its velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Momentum of a body is ____ to its velocity.
e: Momentum of a body is directly proportional to its velocity. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.
Momentum is a vector quantity. Vector quantity here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: Direction of momentum is the same as that of ____.
e: Direction of momentum is the same as that of velocity. Velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Unit of momentum is expressed as the ____.
c: product of mass unit and velocity unit
e: Unit of momentum is expressed as the product of mass unit and velocity unit. Product of mass unit and velocity unit here means an agreed amount you use as the scale of a measurement. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.
In MKS system it is $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.

q: One fundamental law of physics is the ____.
e: One fundamental law of physics is the law of conservation of momentum. Law of conservation of momentum here means mass times velocity, so it is directed. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: This law states that: If there is no net external force acting on an ____, the total momentum of the system is constant.
e: This law states that: If there is no net external force acting on an isolated system, the total momentum of the system is constant. Zero net force means constant velocity, including staying at rest. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: The law of conservation of momentum is a general law and is true for both ____ objects.
e: The law of conservation of momentum is a general law and is true for both macroscopic and microscopic objects. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: According to law of conservation of momentum, ____ = total momentum after collision.
e: According to law of conservation of momentum, Total momentum before collision = total momentum after collision. Total momentum before collision here means mass times velocity, so it is directed. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.
